what_this_is: Hand-made fixture for tools/verdict_v21.py and tools/check_labels_v21.py, lean version 2.1 (guide v2.1 as amended on 2026-10-05: every entry carries the field "saying", and a ^8 or ^9 may be written alone). Every passage and every record in this folder is made up. Every number under "report" was worked out by hand from the records, and so was every line under "printed". The program must print the same numbers. Two things were added after the outside review of 2026-10-05: the strict-label view (a second number beside every E, with no bar) and the reasoning-flag line (report only). Passage F23 was added for them. Run: python -B tools/verdict_v21.py fixture

files.labels_team_a.json.tries.jsonl: team A's try log, one line per try
files.labels_team_b.json.tries.jsonl: team B's try log, one line per try (its first line is not a try and must be skipped)

cases.F01: An exact pair, and one label inside the other. ^1: both teams give the same span. ^9: team A 'her father's workbench in the cellar', team B 'her father's workbench' (inside it; content words father's, workbench are in the longer label). ^8: the two labels are the same span, but the related things differ in the same way. They still agree, and the pair is listed by its loosest field: one inside the other, not same span.
cases.F02: Overlapping spans, no pair: ^2 'the cracked blue jug' against 'blue jug on the sill' overlap, but content words cracked/sill are each missing from the other. Overlap in part, a pair: ^3 'the stack of wet newspapers' against 'stack of wet newspapers by the door'; neither span holds the other, and stack, wet, newspapers are all in the longer label.
cases.F03: The same words at two different places, no pair: both teams write ^2 'the red kite'; team A's support is sentence 1, team B's is sentence 2. The attempt-1 way counts this passage as agreement.
cases.F04: Two entries of one team for one thing, one extra: team B writes ^5 'After twenty years of mending nets' and ^5 'twenty years of mending nets'. Team A's one entry pairs with the exact one (most same-span pairs wins); the other is only B.
cases.F05: An entry only one team wrote: team A's ^4. A wrong related thing where one is required: ^7 with the same label and Mind, related 'fed the hens' against 'the feed bucket': no pair. Team B also lists a second Mind, 'Her cousin': one extra ^1.
cases.F06: A wrong Mind: both teams write ^3 'The stench'; team A's Mind is Brannoc, team B's is Elowen: no pair. Both list both Minds: two ^1 pairs.
cases.F07: An ambiguous entry: team A's ^2 is ambiguous, team B's is clear. Bar row: only B. All-entries table: a pair.
cases.F08: A ^9 reached by reasoning on both sides: outside the ^9 bar row, one pair in the row '^9 reached by reasoning'. ^6: team A names three parts, team B two: two pairs, one only A.
cases.F09: An uncertain pair on both sides (rule 15d): one pair in 'uncertain ^8', one in 'uncertain ^9', nothing in the ^8 and ^9 bar rows. ^5 pairs.
cases.F10: A dropped entry: all three tries of team B hold a ^2 whose label is not inside its support. After the third try the passage is NOT_LABELED and its row is the 'could not be labeled' row. The scorer runs the checker on that last try: 1 entry dropped (the ^2), 2 entries lost with the passage. The passage is left out of every table, for both teams.
cases.F11: A withdrawn entry: team A's first try holds a ^2 with a support that is not a whole sentence; its second try leaves the ^2 out. Counted: 1 withdrawn ^2 for team A.
cases.F12: A passage one team could not label: team B's three tries are not a JSON object, a record with another passage_id, a record with no entries field. The passage is left out of every table. Team B: 2 of 23 not labeled (F10, F12), which is more than 5%, so this fixture run is INVALID.
cases.F13: A passage empty on both sides: both teams say none_of_these. It counts as 'neither' in every row.
cases.F14: The pairing must be a true maximum: team A 'the old brass plumb bob', 'a chalk line', 'a folding rule'; team B 'the old brass plumb bob, a chalk line', 'plumb bob', 'a folding rule'. Pairing A1 with B1 first would leave 'a chalk line' alone (2 pairs). The maximum is 3: A1 with 'plumb bob', 'a chalk line' with B1, and the exact pair.
cases.F15: One label inside the other for ^2: 'the stall with the smoked eel' and 'the smoked eel'. Team A needed two tries: the saying of its first ^2 entry had one word ('Irresistible.'); its second try gives a saying of 2 to 20 words. A corrected saying is not a withdrawn entry: both tries hold the same Noetic, label, Mind and related thing. F15 adds nothing to team A's withdrawn count, and its first try adds 1 entry with a message.
cases.F16: One side empty: team A says none_of_these, team B lists the Mind. ^1: only B; presence: only B.
cases.F17: Full agreement on ^1, ^2 and ^3, all same span. Team B needed two tries: its first ^3 label was not an exact copy ('herrings'), its second try corrects it. A corrected entry is not a withdrawn entry: F17 adds nothing to team B's withdrawn count, and its first try adds 1 entry with a message.
cases.F18: Three things in one passage. (1) A name that stands in two sentences ('Old Nerys ...' and 'Nerys shut ...'). Team B's first try gives the later sentence as the support of its ^1 entry: the checker asks for the first place the name stands, and the four entries that lean on that Mind get a message too (5 entries with a message). Its second try corrects it. (2) One trigger, two things brought to Mind. Team A writes two ^8 entries with the same label and Mind and different related things, and two ^9 entries: the checker lets them stand. Team B's first try holds both pairs, its second try only the first: 1 withdrawn ^8 and 1 withdrawn ^9. The two ^8 entries differ only in relative_to, so the withdrawn count must read that field. Team B's one ^8 can pair only with team A's ^8 that has the same related thing: 1 pair, 1 only A, in the ^8 row and in the ^9 row. (3) A Mind that agrees by the looser test: team A 'Old Nerys', team B 'Nerys'. The ^1 pair, the ^8 pair and the ^9 pair are all listed as one inside the other.
cases.F19: An empty related thing. The passage names parts and never names what they make up. Team A leaves relative_to empty on both ^6 entries and writes a note (guide v1.2 and v2.1). Team B leaves it empty on 'A coil of wire' and fills 'the bench' on 'a spool of solder'. Two empty fields agree: 1 pair, same span. An empty field and a filled field do not agree: 1 only A, 1 only B. No Mind is listed: the passage is 'neither' in every other row.
cases.F20: A lone ^9 on both sides (guide rule 2 as changed on 2026-10-05: a thought that comes with no trigger named). Both teams write ^9 'the blue door of the old boathouse' with relative_to "" and no reached_by. Same label, same Mind, two empty related things: 1 pair in the ^9 bar row, same span. Neither team writes a ^8.
cases.F21: A lone ^9 that only one team wrote: team A writes ^9 'The tune of an old sea song' with relative_to ""; team B lists only the Mind. ^9: 1 only A; presence: only A.
cases.F22: A lone ^9 of one team against a paired ^9 of the other at the same place. Team A writes ^9 'The word for the knot she had forgotten' with relative_to "". Team B writes a pair: ^8 'the ferry horn', and ^9 'The word for the knot she had forgotten' with related thing 'the ferry horn'. The two ^9 labels are the same span and the Minds agree, but an empty and a filled related thing do not agree: no pair. ^9: 1 only A, 1 only B; presence: both. ^8: 1 only B; presence: only B. The attempt-1 way does not count F22 as agreement either.
cases.F23: A conclusion reached by reasoning where one team left the flag out. The passage says the Mind checked, ruled out, 'So it had to be'. Team A writes ^9 'the third fuse' with relative_to "" and no reached_by. Team B writes the same label with reached_by "reasoning". The flag alone decides the row: team A's entry stands in the ^9 bar row (1 only A; presence: only A), team B's in the row '^9 reached by reasoning' (1 only B). They pair only in the all-entries table. The reasoning-flag line lists team A's entry: its support 'So it had to be the third fuse.' holds a word of guide rule 15(b). Team B's entry is not listed: it carries the flag.
cases.saying: The seventh field of an entry (guide v2.1 as amended on 2026-10-05). In the two labels files and the two try logs every entry carries it. It is "" on every ^1 entry. On every other entry it has 2 to 20 words, but for one entry made faulty on purpose: the ^2 of team A's first try of F15. For the same thing the two teams write different sayings, but for two entries: the ^9 of F08 and the ^9 of F09. The scorer never compares the field between the teams, so no pair hangs on it. One saying of the labels files is in the labeler's own words (team A's ^4 in F05); the others are sayings of the map in Part A of the guide, copied exactly. The faulty forms of the field are in checker cases c48 to c59.

worked_by_hand.lone entries: A ^8 or ^9 written alone has relative_to "" and no reached_by (guide rule 2 as changed on 2026-10-05). The checker lets it stand (checker cases c35 and c35b). In the scorer a clear one is an entry of the bar row like any other. Two lone entries pair when their labels and their Minds agree: two empty related things agree (F20). A lone entry does not pair with a paired entry for the same thing: an empty and a filled related thing do not agree (F22). A lone ^9 carries no reached_by, so it is counted in the ^9 bar row and not in the row '^9 reached by reasoning'. The scorer program was not changed for this.

worked_by_hand.strict-label view: The entries are paired again, one to one and with the most pairs that can be made, when two labels may pair only if their spans overlap and they have the same content words in the same order. The Mind and the related thing keep the looser test. M' = those pairs. The number is M' / (A + B - M'). A small word such as 'the', 'a', 'her' or 'by' is not a content word (the list is in tools/verdict.py); "father's" is one word. Bar rows. ^1: M' 17, all but F18 ('Old Nerys' has the content word old, 'Nerys' has not): 17/(18+20-17) = 17/21 = 0.810. ^2: M' 1 (F17; not F15: stall is missing from 'the smoked eel'): 1/(4+5-1) = 1/8 = 0.125. ^3: M' 1 (F17; not F02: door is missing from team A's label): 1/(3+3-1) = 1/5 = 0.200. ^4: 0/1. ^5: M' 2 (F04, where team A's label pairs with team B's same label; F09): 2/(2+3-2) = 2/3 = 0.667. ^6: M' 4 (the bread, the lamp oil, a folding rule, A coil of wire; the two pairs of F14 that hold only by containment are gone): 4/(8+7-4) = 4/11 = 0.364. ^7: 0/2. ^8: M' 2 (F01 and F18: the labels are the same words; the related thing of F01 and the Mind of F18 agree by the looser test, which still stands for them): 2/(3+3-2) = 2/4 = 0.500, the same as E. ^9: M' 2 (F18, F20; not F01: cellar is missing from team B's label): 2/(7+4-2) = 2/9 = 0.222. All entries. ^1 17/21. ^2: M' 2 (F07, F17): 2/(5+5-2) = 2/8 = 0.250. ^3 1/5. ^4 0/1. ^5 2/3. ^6 4/11. ^7 0/2. ^8: M' 3 (F01, F09, F18): 3/(4+4-3) = 3/5 = 0.600. ^9: M' 5 (F08, F09, F18, F20, F23; not F01): 5/(9+7-5) = 5/11 = 0.455. worked_by_hand.reasoning-flag line: The scorer reads the words from rule 15(b) of the guide, after 'Words that show this:'. They are: worked out, checked, ruled out, compared, so it had to be. Counted: the clear ^9 entries with no reached_by, in the 21 analysed passages. Team A has 7 (F01, F18 x2, F20, F21, F22, F23). One of their supports holds a word: F23, 'So it had to be the third fuse.' (capitals are not read). Team B has 4 (F01, F18, F20, F22). None of their supports holds a word. Not counted, because they carry the flag: team B's ^9 of F23 and both teams' ^9 of F08, though their supports hold such words. The line changes no count.
worked_by_hand.floor and intervals: They rest on seeded draws and cannot be worked out by hand in general. Some values can. The ^4 and ^7 floors are 0 in every shuffle (team B has no ^4; a ^7 symbol that moves lands on a Mind entry, and one that stays has the wrong related thing). The ^3 kappa is 1 in every draw that has a value, and about 96% of the draws have one. A row with one case (^4) has no interval: that case is missing from about 36% of the draws, and an interval needs 90%.
worked_by_hand.saying: The field takes no part in any count. Pairing reads the Noetic, the label, the Mind and the related thing. The withdrawn count reads the same four. So a good saying on every entry changes no number of the report. One number does hang on a saying: an entry whose saying has a message counts as an entry with a message. Team A's first try of F15 holds one such entry (a saying of one word), so team A's first tries hold 2 entries with a message: F11's ^2 and F15's ^2. Its second try of F15 passes with the same two entries, so F15 is labeled, nothing is dropped and nothing is withdrawn.
